title: Administrator mode lock
next_action: Approve the elevation-restart design or request the specified failure-time evidence.

judgment.rationale: Persistent administrator mode, manual Run as administrator, and Settings restart-as-administrator all reportedly fail. The attached diagnostic was rejected, so the exact elevation boundary remains unconfirmed.
evidence: PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store on Windows 11 25H2.
Always run as administrator is enabled, but the active process appears non-elevated.
Manual and in-app elevation attempts fail or close/crash PowerToys.
Automated triage reports the attached ZIP contains an oversized entry and was not analyzable.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve focused runner/settings elevation diagnostics and request a fresh failure-time report.

fix_assessment.rationale: No public open or merged fix covers this Store/Windows 11 25H2 elevation failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Make failed administrator relaunches observable and non-silent
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the elevated relaunch starts with --restartedElevated but receives a non-elevated token; runner/main.cpp then intentionally breaks the loop by continuing in user mode, making the setting appear ineffective.
plan: Trace GeneralViewModel.RestartElevated through settings_window.cpp and restart_elevated.cpp.
Capture ShellExecuteEx failure, UAC cancellation, process identity, and relaunch outcome.
Keep the loop-prevention behavior but report failed elevation instead of presenting a successful administrator-mode launch.
Add Store/non-Store and accepted/denied-UAC regression coverage.
verification: Enable Always run as administrator and verify the process token or a visible failure result.
Use Settings > Restart PowerToys as administrator and verify elevated relaunch or explicit failure.
Verify a non-elevated --restartedElevated launch cannot loop indefinitely.

confidence.rationale: The shared relaunch path matches all reported symptoms, but the rejected diagnostic leaves Store packaging, UAC, policy, and token state unresolved.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys remains non-elevated despite administrator mode being enabled, and both manual and Settings-driven elevation fail.
known_information: Affected version is 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store.
Environment is Windows 11 25H2 and the user reports an administrator account.
Always run as administrator is enabled.
Right-click elevation and in-app restart-as-administrator do not produce an elevated session.
The only diagnostic ZIP was rejected by automated triage.
inferences: The common failure likely belongs to the shared runner/settings relaunch path.
A non-elevated --restartedElevated child could explain the apparent fallback to user mode.
Store packaging, UAC, compatibility settings, or policy may instead be the first failing boundary.
issue_context.analysis: The report supports a focused code investigation, but a precise implementation should not be approved as confirmed root cause without usable failure-time diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full body, labels, automated discussion, duplicate reference, and attachment status.
Relevant source paths are GeneralViewModel.RestartElevated, settings_window.cpp restart_elevation handling, restart_elevated.cpp, elevation.h, and runner/main.cpp.
No linked upstream PR or concrete public fix attempt was found.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after one failed administrator-mode attempt.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once, then comment `/bugreport` immediately after PowerToys closes, crashes, or restarts non-elevated.

information_gaps.information: Whether UAC appears and is accepted for each elevation path, plus the Elevated state of PowerToys.exe and PowerToys.Settings.exe.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates launch denial, accepted-UAC fallback, and Settings-only failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Report the UAC result and check the Elevated column in Task Manager Details.

design.root_cause: Unconfirmed failed elevated relaunch followed by the existing non-elevated loop-break path.
evidence: The issue reports failure across persistent, manual, and Settings restart elevation.
runner/main.cpp deliberately continues non-elevated when that argument is present without an elevated token.

affected_files.purpose: Startup elevation decision and loop prevention.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: A successful ShellExecuteEx launch is treated as sufficient.
implementation_steps.change: Return structured launch diagnostics, close process handles, and preserve an explicit failed-relaunch result.
implementation_steps.code_block: auto result = RunElevatedWithDiagnostics(exe, args); if (!result.started) { LogElevationFailure(result.error); return false; }
edge_cases: Do not retry in a loop.
Treat UAC cancellation as a reported failure.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: A non-elevated child continues as a normal user and the UI can still show the persisted preference.
implementation_steps.change: Keep loop prevention but surface failed administrator-mode state distinctly from a successful elevated launch.
edge_cases: Do not clear the persisted preference automatically.

verify: Build runner and Settings with the existing PowerToys Windows workflow.
Repeat persistent, manual, and Settings elevation on Windows 11 25H2.
Confirm either an elevated token or a clear failure result.
risks: Changing restart timing can affect update and Settings reopen flows.
A retry must not recreate the existing elevation loop.
alternatives: Disable administrator mode for Store installs; rejected without evidence.
Always retry elevation; rejected because it risks an infinite loop.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. To resolve the recorded uncertainty, please provide:

1. A fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after one failed administrator-mode attempt. Collection: Reproduce once, then comment `/bugreport` immediately after PowerToys closes, crashes, or restarts non-elevated.
2. Whether UAC appears and is accepted for each elevation path, plus the Elevated state of PowerToys.exe and PowerToys.Settings.exe. Collection: Report the UAC result and check the Elevated column in Task Manager Details.
